abstract: We present a compact, C-based implementation of the Held-Karp dynamic-programming algorithm for the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) that incorporates a balanced search and indexing structure to reduce memory fragmentation and improve spatially localized traversal. The algorithm preserves a strict height-balanced invariant over the implicit binary-mask tree, guaranteeing $O(n^2 2^n)$ time and $O(n 2^n)$ space. Empirical evaluation on an Intel(R) Xeon(R) 6975P-C with 1 physical core and 2 logical threads yields a mean latency of 431.12 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 2,319,551 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261126_030235_improved_quantum_algorithms_fo}.
